R destinations are nested at build.local.<title> or build.github.<title>. Directory sources live at directories.<label>.source, keyed by provider/title, with string title references or inline mappings understood by restore helpers. The source-selection helpers contain defects noted below; not every accepted shape has demonstrated end-to-end behaviour. Destination storage, source getters, restore selection.



Key or entrypoint
Parsed/defaulted/consumed behaviour
Rust status




Title
Named mapping key. Local helper describes title as descriptive; GitHub title becomes release tag. Internal title helper can derive it from content; public wrappers require the title argument. GitHub wrapper replaces spaces with hyphens.
Configured restore uses named references/inline definitions and GitHub tag space/@version normalization; local title remains descriptive.


content
Validates allowed labels; send helper treats null/false as none, true as automatic output/raw/docs, vector as selected labels. Boolean helper support and strict validation are not fully consistent. Cache is not in automatic selection.
Restore accepts false/null, true for declared non-cache roles, or explicit label lists. Build publication remains restricted; no implicit undeclared roles are added.


Special content
R option lists also mention docs/data/code/package; wrappers differ in their allowed sets, and code has special ZIP branches. This is not proof each implicit role works through all send paths.
Preserve approved output-r-data and explicit paths. Do not add implicit code/package/language roles merely from enum text; verify actual packaging route separately.


structure
archive by default; only archive/latest accepted. The wrapper prose saying version is not a supported alias.
Explicit local/GitHub operations and restore support latest/archive. Configured local latest publication executes; ordinary local archive publication now executes; configured GitHub latest/archive covers all inspection/strategy/cue combinations in mocked CLI fixtures, with bounded live verification below.


path
Required for local, anchored at project root when relative. Optional prefix for flat GitHub names.
Local source paths are explicit/root-anchored; compatible GitHub flat-name prefixes exist.


path-append-label
Hyphenated YAML key; defaults true. Snake-case path_append_label is an R argument, not evidence of a YAML alias.
Supported by explicit naming/download and configured restore; default true.


id
Validator accepts it; completion overwrites local id with path and GitHub id with title. Do not mistake it for a freely configurable independent backend id.
Restore accepts a string id but uses local path/GitHub title, matching completion semantics; it is not an independent routing override.


description/id_parent/role
Internal add/check arguments include these legacy fields. Extra-options helper now discards OSF-related extras. No current standalone OSF behaviour follows.
No port required for dead fields without a working source route.


send.cue
if-change by default; enum only if-change/always. never occurs in stale wrapper docs but is rejected by current enum. Title-level cue lookup/setter and nested send.cue differ; see defects.
Both nested cues execute in configured local/GitHub latest/archive across all strategies and inspection modes in mocked CLI fixtures.


send.inspect
manifest by default; file/manifest/none accepted.
Configured local latest supports ordinary MD5 file, default manifest-history comparison/fallback, and none planning. CAS JSON/BLAKE3 checks remain distinct. Ordinary local/GitHub archive comparison is implemented; the complete GitHub control matrix is mocked, with bounded live verification below.


send.strategy
sync-diff default, except inspect:none defaults upload-all. Explicit upload-missing/upload-all/sync-purge/sync-diff preserved.
Configured local latest supports all four strategies and both cues with CSV/VERSION/changelog updates; actual build/store/restore fixtures cover file, none and trusted manifest actions. Local/GitHub latest/archive share the planner; complete GitHub combinations have mocked CLI coverage and bounded live verification below.


send.conflict
Validator accepts overwrite/skip/error, but no store consumer was found.
Accepted-only R surface, not a functioning conflict-policy requirement. Rust must not silently accept an ineffective control.


get.strategy/get.conflict
Accepted/checked; public destination wrappers comment out get arguments. Restore does not consume these policy fields.
Restore rejects nonempty get mappings explicitly instead of pretending the ineffective controls execute. Explicit –clear selects replacement versus merge.


source on destination
Restore permits true (preferred), false (exclude), or label vector (preferred for those labels); content must include the label. If absent, first eligible destination is fallback.
Configured restore implements preferences/exclusion/content eligibility with regression fixtures.


Per-directory source
Source lookup precedes destination lookup by default; pos can restrict source/dest, type and .title restrict selection. Inline/reference default paths are not uniformly reliable.
Existing source-first references and named inline mappings implemented; indexing/inline source bugs are corrected with fixtures.


Settings granularity
Transfer settings are shared per destination title; content labels inherit them. Per-label source mappings choose their own source entries.
Restore resolves per-label sources and shared destination definitions. Configured build/store plans resolve shared title settings and selected labels.


YAML layers
Local overrides active profiles overrides base; earlier listed profiles win; merge recurses, null inherits. R uses _projr base/profile/local names. Merge.
Core merge precedence exists. Deliberate primary _proj.yml plus legacy _projr.yml conflict error retained.


Archive function arguments
archive_local/archive_github accept false/null, true or selected labels; create implicit archive destination only when YAML has no archive title. Existing archive title wins; always_archive controls generated cue. Send dispatch.
Missing compatibility entrypoints. Do not override explicit YAML silently.


Named remote extension
Subsequently approved user design, separate from the original R source behavior.
Issue706 is implemented as top-level remotes plus build.dest, preserving named restore sources and explicit upload label subsets. New style/format/placement behavior is summarized below; legacy inline definitions remain supported.



Actual defaults and checks: destination completion, validation, remote add validation, public wrappers, enums, shipped template.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Store, inspection and metadata
Production/output builds only enter send; previews skip it. GitHub releases can be prepared/created before analysis when configured. Destination parameters and YAML are resolved per title, then labels are processed in content order. Source files for a send come from the project’s current-version manifest, not an unqualified directory listing. The last label also triggers changelog writing. Preparation, send, planner.








Policy
Implemented operation
Required Rust fixture




upload-all
Add every current source-manifest file; no removal of destination-only names. Existing destinations can be marked untrusted.
Existing extra file retained; source overwrite and empty-label cases.


upload-missing
Add names absent remotely; retain existing remote bytes, including changed same-name content.
Same-name different bytes retained; missing names added.


sync-diff
Add missing/changed files, remove remote-only files; compare via chosen inspection.
Add/change/delete transitions and no-change cue.


sync-purge
Clear/recreate destination content then upload full selected set when plan says needed.
Disposable fixture only; never user dataset destructive tests.


inspect:file
Enumerate/hash remote bytes with legacy MD5, compare to project evidence.
Detect actual byte corruption and ignore mtime/size equivalence.


inspect:manifest
Compare recorded rows/version trust. If unavailable/untrusted, planner may fall back to file hashes.
Matching/missing/stale/corrupt metadata and trust markers.


inspect:none
No comparison evidence; default upload-all and untrusted existing-state handling.
Never label unchecked remote bytes verified.


cue
always or change-driven materialisation/version updates; no trust or no prior destination can force creation.
Unchanged inputs under both cues; empty result snapshots.


Exclusions
Cache inventory excludes projr subtree. File listing includes dotfiles. ZIP helpers accept directory include/exclude and exact filename exclusions; filter implementations differ (pathspec vs regex).
Hidden files, nested names, exclusions and empty-after-exclusion; no regex/pathspec interchange assumption.


Execution
Purge, add, remove, reconcile full/empty, then write manifest, VERSION, and optional changelog.
Failure at each boundary must report partial publication honestly.



Plan execution, ZIP helpers, hashing, listing/path filters.
Local metadata is ordinary manifest.csv, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md at the remote pre-root. GitHub uses manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and CHANGELOG.zip containing those files. VERSION has per-label release entries and optional trailing * indicating untrusted state. These files are distinct from CAS JSON and the plural Rust .projr/manifests.csv index. Metadata.
There is no all-or-nothing remote transaction: local copying/removal can be partial, GitHub whole-asset replacement deletes an old asset before uploading, and metadata is written after content. Metadata-download failures may become empty/unavailable state; some unzip errors are swallowed. Rust should retain its approved safety boundaries, surface errors and never claim rollback of remote side effects. HTTP replacement, GitHub transfer.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Versions, listing, downloads and restore








Operation
Source behaviour
Rust comparison




List final remotes
Local immediate child directories; GitHub assets within one configured release.
Explicit local version inspection and GitHub asset listing exist. No cross-release catalogue is promised.


List files
Local recursive listing; GitHub ZIP download/extraction.
Local tree staging and ZIP extraction inspect entries; a separate user-facing recursive list-files command is still absent.


Latest version
latest reads label VERSION entry; archive parses local version-directory/GitHub asset names and selects max semantic version, including empty variants.
Explicit local listing and configured local/GitHub restore select numeric newest/exact archives or advertised latest. Metadata is not an integrity guarantee; current CAS accepts caller-supplied versions.


Trusted version
Stronger helper checks VERSION/archive agreement and project/remote manifest evidence. Restore bypasses this stronger helper.
Missing; do not describe ordinary restore as cryptographically verified.


Download all
Copy directory tree or download named release asset and unzip.
Explicit local/asset/directory downloads and configured single-label restore exist, with staging and exact-byte fixtures.


Download one
Local and GitHub helpers flatten requested file to its basename at destination.
Missing; basename collision handling needs safe bounded implementation rather than unsafe silent overwrite.


Restore labels
Default declared raw labels; explicit labels supported. Root manifest required; empty/unrecorded labels may be skipped.
Ordinary restore retains its root CSV prerequisite and explicit single-label interface. Explicit-ID native CAS verification/recovery does not require the old project CSV/index. Default multi-label raw restore remains missing.


Restore source
Source before destination; filter provider/title/content/source eligibility. First suitable selection, not retry across every provider after failure. Legacy fallback GitHub archive then local _archive exists.
Implemented for explicit single-label restore. Source failures do not silently switch providers. Undeclared archive fallbacks are deliberately excluded by the explicit-mapping contract.


Restore target
Final declared path, safe=false; optional clear removes current contents before lookup/download.
Declared final target and merge/clear are implemented; stage/validate before installation rather than importing clear-before-lookup data loss.


Restore result
Per-label errors can yield partial false; clone wrapper can ignore that false and return true.
Single-label machine results distinguish restored/skipped/failure; stderr retains installation/rollback diagnostics. No multi-label aggregate guarantee is claimed.


Clone wrapper
Clone repo, select/change working directory, invoke content update.
Existing Git-backed init is not a restore clone wrapper.


Most recently modified
Explicit unimplemented helpers; OSF variants explicitly unsupported.
Do not advertise working modification-time source selection.



Version logic, restore, clone wrappers.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Credentials and dependencies
GitHub lower helpers accept explicit token/api_url. Otherwise token lookup is GITHUB_PAT, optional R gh::gh_token, optional gitcreds, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN. API base is explicit override, GITHUB_API_URL, public API. Enterprise gitcreds lookup strips /api/v3; public lookup uses https://github.com. Requests carry an Authorization header and may be unauthenticated without a token. Repository inference prefers origin then first Git remote, using available gh R helpers or system Git/gert. Explicit Enterprise overrides are not forwarded by every wrapper. Authentication, repo inference, HTTP.
These are source mechanisms, not authorisation to obtain new credentials, change permissions or install dependencies. Rust should use supported existing access, mock HTTP for fixtures, redact secrets and never store tokens in CSV/URLs. Current Rust transport accepts explicit API/token inputs; configured restore uses GITHUB_API_URL and existing GITHUB_PAT/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN values. Explicit repository selection avoids Git; inference currently uses origin only and checks its host against the API. R gh/gitcreds fallback and first-other-remote inference remain missing. R helper auto-install behaviour is not adopted. Real Git remains an optional installed dependency; GitHub CLI is separate and need not be mandatory for an API implementation. Optional managed Git is not planned by default.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Source defects and documentation-only surfaces
These are source-review findings, not executed reproductions or requirements to copy bugs. Keep claims bounded until fixture evidence exists.

Default source selection passes an inner mapping where the next helper expects the provider mapping; explicit provider selection can call a title-specific helper with a null title. Selection.
GitHub existence checks hard-code label/version names, ignoring some custom path/append-label settings; local archive discovery assumes a label directory. GitHub existence, version paths.
Title send-check reads top-level cue while defaults populate send.cue; the cue setter also writes a different level. Send, defaults.
get/conflict fields are validated but no effective execution consumer was found. wrapper docs mention never/version and OSF, outside actual enums.
GitHub unzip failures can be swallowed, clone restore ignores partial failure, and low-level asset deletion can infer the current repo despite a repo argument. GitHub, HTTP, clone.
Content option sets, wrapper checks and boolean auto-content helpers differ; special code/package labels alone do not prove working end-to-end export.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
section: Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility
text:
Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility
This assessment excludes the agreed temporary CSV choice. Examples use the existing R inline build configuration, not a newly approved Rust schema. Findings are source-backed; unless stated otherwise they are not executed reproductions. Proposed fixes are review candidates, not silent semantic changes.



Rank/type
Example and user impact
Smallest proposed fix




High: ineffective accepted setting
A destination with send: {conflict: skip} passes allowed-value checks, but store execution never reads conflict. get: {strategy: upload-missing, conflict: error} similarly has no restore consumer. Users can believe a non-overwrite policy is enforced. Checks, execution.
Reject ineffective combinations until implemented, or implement and test them explicitly. Do not silently ignore a safety control.


High: colliding-target combination
build.local.shared with content: [raw-a, raw-b], structure: latest, path-append-label: false, send: {inspect: file, strategy: sync-diff} gives both labels one physical directory. File inspection can classify the other label’s files as extras. Custom archive/pre-root paths also assume layouts not uniformly supported. Layout, planner, versions.
Resolve all target identities before mutation and reject collisions; verify supported custom-prefix/append combinations rather than accepting untested layouts.


High: destructive restore ordering
A normal configured restore source plus projr_content_update(clear=TRUE) clears the destination before source resolution/download. A missing release or failed network call can leave data gone. clear defaults FALSE; this is an unsafe opt-in ordering, not an unsafe default. Restore.
Download into private staging, validate, then apply guarded promotion. Preserve current data on lookup/download failure.


Medium: surprising default synchronisation
build.local.shared: {path: backup, structure: latest, content: [output]} defaults to sync-diff, so remote-only files can be removed. A user expecting an additive backup may be surprised. Default archive keeps prior version directories, which narrows the risk. Defaults, planner.
Clearly expose adds/removes and the resolved strategy before applying; require deliberate review before changing defaults. This is a usability/policy concern, not evidence that sync-diff itself is defective.


Medium: profile cannot disable with null
Base build.github.archive selects output; a local/profile build.github.archive: null inherits the base mapping. Removing one active-profile destination also does not remove its base definition. Merge.
Explain merged effective destinations and provide a deliberately designed disabling/empty-selection mechanism. Do not reinterpret null without an approved compatibility change.


Medium: argument precedence surprise
YAML build.local.archive: {content: [raw-a], path: backup} means archive_local=c(‘raw-b’) does not replace that archive definition. always_archive also defers to explicit archive YAML. Dispatch.
Document this as YAML authority and display the resolved content; avoid presenting these arguments as ordinary overrides. Whether arguments should override is a design choice.


Medium: two cue locations
send: {cue: always} is completed and used per label, while title-level send checking and the setter reference top-level cue. This invites inconsistent getter/setter behaviour; nested cue is not simply unused. Send, defaults.
Use one canonical nested location and test the public setter through an actual store plan; treat an alias only through explicit conflict rules.


Medium: provider-dependent identity
build.github.nightly: {id: another-tag, content: [output]} validates an id, but completion resets it to nightly. Local id instead becomes path. Title is cosmetic locally and functional on GitHub. Completion.
Reject or clearly deprecate ignored id values; document title/tag/path meanings. A larger unified identity design is separate.


Medium: source-selection defects
directories.raw-data.source: {github: archive}, as shipped in the template, meets default helper paths that pass the wrong mapping level or an absent title into a title-specific branch. Template, selection.
Fix source selection with explicit/default provider/title fixtures; do not require users to discover accidental nesting workarounds.


Medium: unsupported documentation
send.cue: never and structure: version are mentioned in wrappers but excluded by current enums; old OSF prose outlives implementation. Wrappers, enums.
Correct docs and errors. Implement new values only if separately requested, not to make stale prose true.


Already recorded design
Removing a build destination can remove a historical restore source because definitions and upload selection share the same location.
The original registry proposal is issue706. Named definitions and independent ordinary upload/source lookup are now implemented in PR211; per-remote placement, flat/tree style and CSV/JSON format integration are now included in the development extension below. The source audit itself did not implement it.


Low: naming preference
dest versus destinations changes readability, not provider or safety behaviour.
The approved selection key is build.dest. No destinations alias or silent legacy migration was introduced.



Credential lookup also deserves explicit presentation: ambient R gh/gitcreds resolution precedes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, and repository inference may choose origin or the first remote. A supplied environment token or repository can therefore differ from a user’s expectation. The smallest safe improvement is clear resolved host/repository diagnostics without secrets, plus tests for explicit overrides; no new credential permissions are implied.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
section: Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence
text:
Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence
Test sources were inspected without running R. Fixtures must establish behaviour before fixes are claimed; a source test title alone is not an acceptance result.







Source coverage
What it establishes here




test-yml-dest, test-yml-dest-wrapper, test-yml-remote-check
Parser/default/helper assertions exist, including accepted values. Not run in this audit.


test-dest-send, test-dest-send-label, test-dest-send-prepare
Dispatch/planner/version/empty helper coverage exists. Not whole-provider publication evidence.


test-remote-dispatcher, test-remote-local, test-remote-versions-local
Local dispatcher/layout/transfer/version fixtures exist. Reproduce equivalent Rust fixtures remotely.


test-remote-github
Tests require mutable credentials and explicitly skip GitHub Actions. Presence is not CI coverage. Prefer safe mocked REST/ZIP fixtures for Rust.


test-restore, test-restore-coverage, test-restore-repo
Restore selection/validation/clone test intent; source defects above still require targeted witnesses.


Existing Rust CAS tests
Prove bounded BLAKE3 object/JSON/index behaviour, not ordinary latest/archive parity.


PR175 CSV tests
Production pre/post MD5/history, strict encoding, exclusions and recovery; separate exact-head CI/review evidence on that PR.



Remaining slices should stay independently testable:

Remaining ordinary publication compatibility, including local configured path-append-label:false. Latest/archive cue/inspection/strategy planning, metadata history, empty variants and namespace preflight are delivered; preserve that complete tested matrix while filling the bounded gaps.
Remaining restore conveniences and compatibility: default multi-label raw restore, individual-file extraction, credential-helper fallback and repository inference beyond origin. Retain source-first selection and guarded installation.
CAS-specific archive integration where the existing structures do not decide snapshot discovery/retention. Isolate those decisions from ordinary parity; issue706’s named remote definitions/upload selection are now implemented; broader discovery/retention remains deferred.

The full inventory stays open until implemented and independently reviewed evidence maps every supported row. CSV completion alone closes none of the broader provenance/remote milestones. The subsequently approved registry is documented below. It is an intentional extension, not an accidental reinterpretation of old inline definitions.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Current command reference
See the remote command reference for the delivered local inspection/download/store, GitHub asset/ZIP/replacement and configured restore commands, limits and failure boundaries. The compatibility log retains per-slice source comparisons, review findings and verification evidence.
Machine restore stdout has a static structured failure. Stderr carries the operational diagnostic chain, including paths and parser details; it is not a general configuration-redaction boundary. HTTP errors omit credentials and response bodies. Empty/unrecorded labels skip without clearing, and successful CSV/version selection is not a byte-integrity guarantee.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Configured local publication
Configured local latest/archive publication includes all four strategies, both cues and file/manifest/none inspection, namespace preflight and shared CSV/VERSION/changelog updates. The control matrix describes delivered behavior. PR185 and subsequent reviewed slices record the incremental evidence; the complete preview.3 delivery and remaining limits are linked above.
Pinned R comparison: dest-send-label.R355,854-1560,1587-1788 and manifest.R67-75,192-225 in the source revision linked above. New empty labels and file-equal missing/starred metadata receive explicit discoverability corrections; these are documented differences rather than claims that the pinned R no-change path already repairs them. The original publication slices did not adopt registry or unresolved policy changes. The subsequent registry/tree work is recorded below.
Local archive publication includes complete versioned snapshots, historical reuse eligibility and actual build/store/restore coverage. Configured GitHub publication is delivered as described below. Local configured path-append-label:false remains pending; no full remote-completion claim.
Configured GitHub latest/archive publication supports file/manifest/none inspection and all four strategies, including missing Release creation, CSV data ZIPs and shared metadata history. Canonical current-data replacement merges selected files while preserving remote extras. Empty sources preserve existing targets; validated empty-to-full transitions remove the obsolete sentinel asset after upload. Its PR records mocked REST CLI round-trip evidence. File/manifest and historical comparison use the same staged ordinary planner as local remotes; the command reference records the full control matrix and source-backed blind missing/diff and bounded purge interactions. A dedicated live configured-publication round-trip is now verified below; the full decision matrix remains mocked REST coverage.
The comparison candidate preserves the existing archive/manifest/sync-diff/ if-change defaults. Reuse requires newest catalog/VERSION/matching CSV agreement and continuous unchanged history. Physical file fallback, trusted partial manifest semantics, complete new snapshots and corrupt-empty rejection have actual CLI mock REST regression fixtures. Exact-head remote CI and independent review remain required for later changes; the completed source gates are recorded on PR194. This does not complete all provider options or M2.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Live GitHub fixture verification
A real GitHub round-trip passed using the source build at 03074c8. The dedicated fixture prerelease contains synthetic CSV files only. It is not a product release or an installation target. The verification report records exact binary, artifact and asset hashes; no credentials or local private paths are included.
The isolated CI binary executed five no-script builds and two configured restores:







Step
Verified result




Latest v1.2.4
Native data and shared metadata ZIPs uploaded


Latest v1.2.5
Selected data replaced; exact bytes restored


Archive v1.2.6
Complete versioned snapshot created


Unchanged project v1.2.7
Data reused from v1.2.6; Project metadata advanced


Changed archive v1.2.8
Complete newer snapshot restored; old archive and latest ZIP bytes unchanged



Checks compared exact ZIP members, remote CSV serialization and complete project history rows, VERSION and file bytes. Restore preserved project CSV/VERSION and remote asset identities/hashes. The Release identity, tag commit, prerelease status and fixture-only asset names were checked throughout. No Git commits/push, existing user assets, credentials or permissions were changed.
This real witness covers file/sync-diff/latest and manifest/sync-diff/archive with if-change. The full inspection/strategy/cue/layout and failure matrix is tested separately with mocked REST; it is not a live test of every combination. The published preview.3 packages these source changes and is now installed in the verified WSL location; see delivery evidence. The fixture’s package version string is also preview.2, so identify the tested source by its commit and binary hash, not that string alone.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Current preview.4 delivery
The original source audit and historical rollout notes below remain useful compatibility evidence. Preview.4 includes the following reviewed M3 features and is installed in WSL; see verified release evidence.
Defaults below apply to named top-level remote definitions. Legacy inline ordinary definitions without new metadata fields retain their opt-in behavior; legacy CAS name-list definitions keep their old flat encoding. Stored snapshots remain readable independently of the current write style.








Destination/data layout
File-list choices
Recovery boundary




Native local content-addressed archive
Tree JSON by default; flat CSV/JSON and optional file dictionaries.
Explicit snapshot-ID verification and staged single-label recovery; full remote metadata can recover without the old project. Legacy flat IDs remain readable.


Ordinary local latest/archive folders
Flat CSV by default; all four flat formats or explicit tree JSON.
Existing compatible CSV/VERSION restore and physical folders; do not interpret ordinary bindings as native CAS snapshots.


GitHub Release latest/archive ZIPs
Flat CSV by default; all four flat formats or explicit tree JSON in a bounded metadata ZIP.
Existing compatible ZIP/CSV/VERSION restore. New format coverage is mocked REST with actual CLI execution, not a new live-format round-trip.



Named top-level remotes remain available as sources after removal from build.dest. Build selection may limit logical folder labels without deleting definitions. Per-remote manifest placement chooses project/remote/both full metadata copies; auto uses remote for native CAS and both for ordinary layouts. Small project references remain even with remote full listings. Existing root ordinary manifest.csv and compatible transport metadata retain their separate meanings.
Plain csv/json deduplicate unchanged artefact versions by direct references to earlier complete inventories. Optional csv-dedupe-file/json-dedupe-file also use file dictionaries while retaining every path row. Tree style is fixed JSON, with pure directory identities independent of label/version/physical location. Old snapshots and compatible histories survive style/format changes.
See the configuration reference, remote commands, practical guide and lifecycle. The integrated local M3 gate retains actual archives/recovered bytes and corruption failures, verified by a separate Rust witness; exact release gates and installation are separate. Default multi-label restore, individual-file/list/trusted-version conveniences, additional credential inference, automatic CAS discovery and performance work remain follow-ups. The unchanged R package is the source comparison, not an implementation target for these new configuration/metadata choices.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
section: Current development extensions beyond the original audit
text:
Current development extensions beyond the original audit
PR211 added named ordinary definitions and upload subsets independently of restore sources. PR212 added configured local recursive-tree publication and metadata placement, preserving legacy flat CAS identities. These extend projr; they do not establish complete parity with every convenience wrapper or option.
The following explicit named-ID CAS recovery/verification slice reuses the tree verifier and guarded installer without root CSV, current upload selection or a project ledger. Ordinary restore still uses its documented CSV/version/source selection. Legacy flat CAS compatibility recovery is described in the current command reference. Runtime flat CSV/JSON publication is now implemented as described below. The configuration, remote commands and compatibility log distinguish implemented and pending work.
The local CAS flat catalogue extension now connects CSV/JSON and optional file dictionaries to publication/recovery. Ordinary local and GitHub Release format integration is also implemented in the current development extension below. See the configuration reference.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
WarningTry it on a disposable project



Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds (proj build) can modify or remove files. Recovery covers only recorded managed paths. Never run production builds on the only copy of important work. Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
1. Make a small project
In an Ubuntu terminal, choose a new folder and open it:
mkdir projcli-example
cd projcli-example
Create a file named _proj.yml with this content:
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
The paths are explicit: runtime does not supply missing mappings or invent undeclared labels.








Label
Folder
Role in this example




raw-data
_raw_data
Input files; unused because our three measurements are built into the script.


cache
_tmp
Temporary results; the script writes inside _tmp/preview.


output
_output
Result files; unused by this preview.



Only cache is used by this Python example. The other two mappings match the local initializer’s preset. No docs path is implied: document rendering needs an explicit docs mapping too.
The explicit build.scripts list selects our one script. No Git setup, remote repository or initialization command is needed for this manual setup.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
2. Add an analysis
Create analysis.py in the same folder:
import csv
import os
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

root = Path(os.environ["PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT"])
preview = root / "_tmp" / "preview"
preview.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

measurements = [10, 12, 14]
result = preview / "summary.csv"
with result.open("w", newline="") as handle:
    writer = csv.writer(handle)
    writer.writerow(["count", "mean"])
    writer.writerow([len(measurements), mean(measurements)])

print(f"Saved {result}")
The three measurements are deliberately built into the script so there is no data download or extra package installation. The script uses the project root provided by projcli and explicitly writes to _tmp/preview.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
3. Check, then run
proj --project . yml read
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
cat _tmp/preview/summary.csv
The CSV should contain:
count,mean
3,12
The validation command reads configuration. The preview runs the script. Running it again replaces this example’s CSV; change a measurement and rerun to see the mean change.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
4. Understand what changed
The script creates _tmp/preview/summary.csv. The CLI does not create a VERSION file, publish to docs, or export an archive during this preview.
A preview is not a sandbox: your script can still write elsewhere if you tell it to. Keep preview writes in an explicit temporary folder.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
Starting another project
In another new project folder, local-only directory setup is available:
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories
When no base or active profile configuration exists, this writes _proj.yml with the explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp and output: _output paths, creates those folders, and updates ignore files. It does not run Git or GitHub setup. Existing configuration files are preserved; only their declared directories are created.
The generated file omits build.scripts, allowing the normal shallow script discovery. To choose an exact analysis, add a scripts list as above. An explicit scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts; hooks can still run. Initialization does not turn an absent scripts key into an empty list.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
Where to go next

Query a declared path with proj --project . path get --label cache.
Add your own script to build.scripts.
Read the build reference before using proj build. Production builds have different version, cleanup and export behavior.
Check what works before adding document rendering or R tooling.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Preview.4 includes the named remote definitions, file-history formats and explicit local snapshot recovery documented below. Historical slice notes retain their original verification scope. See verified delivery.
Preview.4 includes named remotes, local tree/flat CAS and explicit verified recovery. The final sections describe implemented local CSV/JSON history. Earlier dated codec sections record the initial library slices. Automatic snapshot lookup and optional DVC remain separate work. Ordinary local/GitHub flat history is implemented in the final sections. These additions are included in preview.4.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Standalone ordinary use
proj must work with its own native backend without installing DVC. DVC must not become the mandatory manifest engine or a dependency of ordinary proj use. Existing interpreter and renderer requirements still apply to selected analyses.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Optional DVC-backed directories
Future integration may let users opt individual directories into DVC backing. Only users selecting that integration need DVC. proj should automatically delegate the appropriate operations at the agreed lifecycle points.
proj retains its logical directory labels/roles and path abstraction regardless of backend. Integration must preserve label resolution so analysis code does not depend on DVC-specific physical paths.
DVC remains authoritative for its own tracking and cache state. proj references the corresponding versions rather than maintaining a second authoritative copy of DVC’s data/cache inventory. Projects should be able to mix native and DVC-backed directories. Missing DVC, unavailable data and delegation failures need explicit handling; proj must not silently install DVC.
The directory configuration, supported restore/build/store operations, exact hook timing and failure/recovery boundaries still need design. This note does not adopt old command recipes or decide a provider contract.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
A curated release catalogue
The intended release catalogue is a curated, linear history on the main branch, presented as a readable changelog. A general catalogue of every run on every branch is not the product goal. This direction does not change current build or Git branch policies, or remove the need to report failed attempts honestly.
Attempt/release identity, allocation, sealing and how failures relate to this catalogue remain open. Temporary legacy CSV is approved below. Durable recording architecture, remote-only discovery, retention and Git-tracking policy remain open; this note does not claim M2 completion.
See the behavior contract, current lifecycle and compatibility log for implemented behavior and limits.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Compatible CSV inventory
Status: this CSV implementation is included in published preview.3. The user approved temporary projr-compatible CSV while broader recording design continues. This supersedes deferring every manifest implementation.
The root manifest.csv contains quoted string columns in this order: label,fn,version,hash. The filename is relative to its declared directory with slash separators, version includes v, and hash is the lowercase MD5 of file bytes. An empty or absent declared directory has one row with blank filename and hash. MD5 provides legacy comparison compatibility, not authenticity or security.
Production captures hash-enabled raw/cache directories before analysis, after start hooks and preparation. Cache capture excludes its framework-owned projr subtree. After successful output promotion it captures hash-enabled output/docs, then writes those snapshots followed by prior history. Exact duplicate rows are omitted; different versions retain records. With no eligible cache the pre-state stays in memory; otherwise it is also saved at <selected-cache>/projr/<release-version>/manifest.csv. No mapping is invented. Explicit empty analysis can inventory existing artifacts without claiming analysis ran.
Existing history must have the four columns in order and valid rows; corruption fails before hooks instead of being discarded. New CSV writes use guarded same-directory replacement, preserving hard-link aliases. Failure before publication restores root CSV bytes/presence with managed state. Publication failure retains the successful local release and CSV. Cache residue may remain. Previews do not produce production records.
This is an inventory at two lifecycle points, not sealing, environment capture, immutable attempt identity, concurrent snapshot or complete provenance. End hooks run later and may change artifacts. The codec is isolated from build capture for later replacement. CSV has no dependency on CAS. The existing plural .projr/manifests.csv CAS index and remote JSON/objects remain separate, unchanged.

Remote layout direction
projr separates provider configuration from latest/archive layouts. Local providers use path[/label] and path[/label]/v<version>. Store planning includes inspection, cues and sync strategies; restore selects available label versions and copies into final paths. Compatibility includes more than copying a manifest.
Working interpretation: retain ordinary latest/archive and add CAS as a third remote structure, with versioned snapshots and content-addressed objects. CAS can provide archive storage without becoming the manifest format. Current Rust runtime now includes ordinary local and GitHub latest/archive publication, inspection and staged configured restore, plus the older local flat-CAS ingestion and integrity APIs. Those delivered transfers are not new M3 work. M3 adds the missing CAS recovery/safety and the now-approved versioned flat/tree metadata; the first codec slice below does not yet wire new configuration or transfer APIs. There is no DVC dependency, destructive migration, garbage collection or performance claim. Ordinary root manifest.csv remains separate from the legacy CAS lookup ledger .projr/manifests.csv.
Pinned reference: manifest, hashing, build capture, defaults, layouts, store, restore.
Existing opt-in Git commit behavior still stages eligible project files, including root CSV unless ignored. This adds no automatic Git requirement or ignore rule. All regular files, including dotfiles, are inventoried; exact R enumeration parity beyond the stated schema/capture comparison remains unverified.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
section: Approved M3 direction and current source boundary
text:
Approved M3 direction and current source boundary
There is one project per store for this milestone. A remote’s existing flat CAS manifest already contains its label, version and all file paths/hashes. The project-local plural ledger is a lookup shortcut, not the sole holder of that metadata. Explicit snapshot selection can read remote metadata directly; a label/version lookup must report missing or conflicting candidates instead of silently picking one. Automatic discovery improvements and performance tuning are deferred rather than treated as proof that metadata is absent.
Four choices remain distinct:








Choice
Meaning
Approved direction




Provider
How bytes travel
Existing local filesystem or GitHub Releases.


Layout
Where payload bytes live
Preserve latest/archive; CAS is an additional structure.


Manifest style
How a snapshot’s names/content identities are described
flat or recursive tree; defaults flat for GitHub/non-CAS local, tree for CAS; explicit per-remote override.


Manifest placement
Where recovery metadata is retained
auto/project/remote/both; auto uses remote for CAS and existing latest/archive behaviour. A small Git root reference can remain even with remote metadata.



The remotes registry and build.dest selection are approved integration work. Omitting a selected remote’s directory subset means all eligible directories; removing it from upload targets must not remove it as a restore source. These new fields are not accepted by the current parser in this codec-only slice. Legacy configurations and data are not silently converted.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Versioned codecs in development source
The Rust snapshot_format module introduces three explicit JSON schemas:

projcli.flat-snapshot.v1: one complete snapshot, with shared version/date metadata once and complete file lists grouped by logical label.
projcli.directory-tree.v1: one directory’s direct child name/type/hash entries. A child is a file or another tree; no logical label or release metadata is in this content object.
projcli.tree-snapshot.v1: the small version/date and label-to-root associations, separate from the directory content IDs.

New file rows name BLAKE3 as their algorithm. Existing ordinary manifest.csv keeps its four-column MD5 semantics. Existing flat CAS manifests retain their old label/version-bearing JSON and raw-byte identities; a bare legacy ID is never automatically interpreted as a new directory tree. This slice adds codecs, not a destructive conversion or a replacement of either legacy reader.
Flat JSON prints each complete path/hash entry and empty-directory leaf on its own line. Empty logical roots remain visible even with no files. Other directory parents are visible in their paths. There are no cross-version deltas or hidden references needed to inspect the complete flat file list. JSON grouping does not make this a recursive tree and does not promise smaller files than CSV.
Directory trees bind direct names, file/tree types and child hashes. Changing a label, build version or supplied date changes snapshot metadata, not the directory root. A new file changes its content hash and relevant ancestors; independent unchanged subtrees can retain their IDs. Permissions, ownership and filesystem timestamps are not part of this byte/name identity.
All new IDs use BLAKE3 derive-key mode with their exact schema string as context, over compact canonical UTF-8 JSON. Struct fields have fixed order; labels, file paths, empty-directory leaves and tree children are sorted by UTF-8 bytes. A supplied RFC3339 date is normalized to UTC; none means unknown and never queries the clock. Version/date metadata is part of snapshot identity, while pretty spacing/line endings and input ordering are not. New format versions must not silently change this canonical encoding.
Readers reject unknown schemas/fields, invalid hashes, duplicate or portable case/normalization aliases, traversal, device names and conflicting file/empty directory shapes. Bounds are 16 MiB JSON, 8 MiB text, 100,000 flat entries or direct children, 4,096 logical labels, 4,096-byte paths with at most 64 components, and 1,024-byte names/labels. Flat prefix expansion has its own global 16 MiB work budget checked before allocating derived prefixes.
Not yet delivered by these codecs: source ingestion, immutable tree-object publication, graph traversal/deep verification, restore installation, registry selection, manifest placement or automatic Git root-reference writes. Those consumers must verify every object’s canonical identity before following references, bound both graph work and expanded output paths, and publish snapshot references last. Equal canonical identities must never authorize overwriting different stored bytes without verified semantic equivalence. Ordinary transfer and the M2 managed recovery pipeline remain unchanged.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
section: Targeted lessons, without importing another tool’s contract
text:
Targeted lessons, without importing another tool’s contract
Git’s objects documentation illustrates the separation between file contents, named tree edges and commit metadata. This is an engineering lesson, not Git-object-format compatibility: proj’s algorithms, encoding and filesystem metadata scope are stated above.
DVC’s cache documentation shows content deduplication and a directory descriptor containing relative path/hash entries. Deduplication is independent of whether a manifest is flat or recursive; grouped JSON alone is not a recursive tree. DVC remains optional future integration, not a runtime dependency.
Packit’s primary description of outpack packets separates analysis files from associated metadata. Existing M2 attempt/provenance records serve that different purpose; a content root is not a scientific result, a complete run catalogue or proof of reproducibility.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
section: Local tree-object APIs in development source
text:
Local tree-object APIs in development source
The cas_tree library now connects the codecs to explicit local storage roots. This is not new configuration activation or a claim that the CLI can restore tree snapshots yet. Callers choose a file-content base and a metadata base; equal bases keep recovery metadata with the content, while different bases permit project-side metadata without changing content-root IDs.
For a 64-character digest beginning ab, paths are:







Object
Path below its selected base




Raw file bytes, shared with the old CAS
objects/ab/remaining-62-hex


V1 directory object
trees/v1/ab/remaining-62-hex.json


V1 snapshot reference
tree-snapshots/v1/ab/remaining-62-hex.json


Existing legacy flat manifest
manifests/full-64-hex.json, unchanged



The legacy flat lookup ledger is still project .projr/manifests.csv. New explicit tree reads do not require it or a working project copy: remote references and their tree graph contain version/label/name/hash information. The old public flat verifier remains a separate legacy reader. A missing/empty legacy manifest directory now fails rather than claiming an archive was verified; an explicit empty snapshot is valid. Deep legacy errors distinguish missing/nonregular objects from corrupt bytes.
ingest_directory pre-scans the selected source and rejects links, special files, unsafe names, source/storage overlap and project control aliases before store publication. It rechecks each file at open and hashes the same stream that is copied. It returns an immutable content root, not a published successful snapshot. It does not silently filter hidden files or produce an atomic consistent image of a concurrently edited dataset.
publish_snapshot verifies every referenced directory ID and actual file bytes before atomically installing the immutable reference. Identical supplied metadata is idempotent. Existing JSON with harmless formatting differences is validated against the same canonical ID and reused without rewriting it. Concurrent equal references may converge safely; there is no mutable latest index or implicit clock in these APIs. Errors can leave unreferenced immutable objects, not a successful reference to an incomplete graph. No cleanup/GC or cross-location transaction is promised.
verify_snapshot is read-only and takes an explicit snapshot ID. It checks typed schemas, object identity, regular/no-link paths and file hashes, and returns complete observed file/empty-directory membership per label. A small reference file alone is not sufficient proof that an archive is intact. Metadata is bounded to 16 MiB per object and 64 MiB unique graph metadata; traversal also caps depth 64, expanded entries 100,000 and expanded path text 16 MiB. DAG reuse does not bypass the expanded-output limits. Permission/ownership/timestamp restoration and live-dataset consistency are outside this byte/name observation.
A caller can request a complete readable JSON inventory export, subject to the separate flat-view bounds. It never substitutes a truncated list. This export does not select the stored flat catalogue policy.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
section: Revised flat catalogue direction: CSV and JSON
text:
Revised flat catalogue direction: CSV and JSON
The later user decision keeps both CSV and JSON. Default csv/json catalogues will deduplicate complete inventories at the logical artefact/version level: an unchanged later version directly references an earlier complete inventory. This is distinct from flat/tree structure and raw file-object CAS deduplication.
Optional csv-dedupe-file and json-dedupe-file modes are off by default. Their dictionary representation must retain every current path membership, resolve to full verified hashes, and not become omitted-file deltas. CSV must remain a rectangular Excel-filter-friendly table. A reference row will identify the earlier complete version; filtering only that later row does not magically expand the earlier file list.
Those catalogue serializers/reference rules are not wired by this tree-object slice. The existing complete JSON codec is a full inventory/view primitive; it is not a JSON-only default or a decision to drop legacy CSV. Existing root ordinary manifest.csv, old flat CAS data and their readers remain compatible.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
section: Version-reference catalogue codecs in development source
text:
Version-reference catalogue codecs in development source
The new catalogue library keeps CSV and JSON and provides four explicit serialization modes: csv, json, csv-dedupe-file and json-dedupe-file. These codecs do not yet select a remote’s write format, change active configuration, replace the root projr manifest.csv or migrate existing flat CAS snapshots.
Default csv/json append an unchanged logical artefact as a direct reference to the earliest complete same-label inventory already in that catalogue. A changed version has a complete inventory. Reverting to old bytes can reference that older complete version; references never target other references. Existing records are not overwritten. Record append order expresses history; no lexical version/date ordering is inferred. Duplicate label/version records, forward/dangling/cross-label references and digest mismatches fail.
Inventory equality binds canonical sorted portable paths, entry kinds, full file BLAKE3 digests and explicit empty-directory leaves. Version, date, logical label and physical root are outside that inventory digest; reference lookup still requires the same logical label. The identity domain is projcli.artefact-inventory.v1 over compact fixed-field JSON containing files and empty_directories, after the existing flat-path validation. Raw file hashes, directory-tree IDs and snapshot/reference IDs retain their different domains.
JSON has an explicit projcli.flat-catalogue.v1 schema, format and hash_algorithm. Each record contains label, version, optional normalized created_at, inventory_hash and an inventory tagged as complete or reference. A reference has ref_version and cannot mix in file rows.
CSV has one rectangular header:
schema, format, hash_algorithm, record, record_index, label, version, created_at, inventory_hash, path, hash, ref_version, file_id.
The record column distinguishes catalogue metadata, inventory, file, empty_directory, reference and dictionary rows. Explicit inventory rows represent empty roots too. File membership rows repeat label/version metadata deliberately: an Excel table filter on a complete artefact/version shows all its file paths. A reference row names the earlier version to filter; filtering only the later version does not expand its referenced inventory. record_index keeps append order explicit even if a spreadsheet sorts rows. CSV quoting preserves commas, quotes and Unicode rather than changing the recorded path. Import text columns as text in spreadsheet software; CSV does not control its formula interpretation.
The opt-in file-dedupe modes bundle one dictionary of distinct full file digests. They retain every path membership row, replacing only repeated hashes with document-local integer file_id values. IDs are assigned deterministically by sorted full digest for each export; they are not persistent global identities. Parsing resolves them to full hashes, verifies complete inventory digests and rejects duplicate/unused/dangling dictionary entries or mixed hash/ID membership. Exports contain their own dictionary, not references to another database.
These are bounded metadata codecs, not proof that physical objects exist. Documents cap at 16 MiB, text at 8 MiB, and complete membership/history/dictionary rows at 100,000; existing path/depth/alias checks still apply. No size or speed advantage is claimed. Catalogue publication dependency ordering, immutable remote integration and no-code expanded listing remain integration work.
Independent review tightened the catalogue-wide limits: dictionary plus membership rows count before JSON expansion, derived path-prefix work shares one 16 MiB budget across history, and CSV/JSON output stops at the byte limit while writing. A transient earliest-complete lookup avoids rescanning all history for each new selected label; it adds no persistent index.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Verified local tree recovery APIs
The restore_label library API accepts explicit content/metadata bases, a v1 snapshot ID, one exact logical label and an absolute destination whose parent already exists. It does not infer latest/history candidates or require the old project ledger. It deeply verifies the full snapshot, materialises selected bytes into owned private staging, hashes the copied stream and verifies actual private stage bytes/membership again before replacing the destination.
Recovery reuses the ordinary guarded directory installer and its bounded rollback. With clear=false, destination-only files survive; matching selected files receive the selected bytes, and selected empty directories may retain destination-only children. With clear=true, final membership matches the selected inventory, including explicit empty directories. The result reports clear and the selected snapshot/version/label. No project VERSION or source/store bytes are updated.
Project authorities/control aliases, linked/special destinations and overlap with CAS objects/tree/reference namespaces fail. Empty snapshots need no objects directory. Remote metadata supports recovery into a fresh empty working project; project-side metadata remains supported when that metadata still exists.
A new internal installer verification callback runs on its private next-stage before retaining the previous destination. Existing ordinary local/GitHub paths use the same installer with their previous behavior. No hard-linked external file inode is edited in place.
The recovery API remains explicitly selected. Named registry and configured tree publication/placement are described below; automatic snapshot selection and flat catalogue publication integration remain pending. Explicit configured verification/recovery is described below. It is not a crash-atomic transaction or arbitrary concurrent-writer sandbox. Permissions/ownership restoration is not a CAS guarantee. As with the ordinary installer, cleanup failure can report an installed destination and retained private backup rather than pretending rollback after successful installation.
Source review added explicit legacy manifests namespace protection: a tree restore cannot target the old flat manifests directory either. Merge validation compares actual directory-entry spelling, including selected empty directories, so native case aliases cannot widen an existing private directory’s modes.
Both private staging levels are explicitly closed. If a pre-replacement callback rejects a copied tree, cleanup may unlock only owned copies, never the installed destination or a retained previous original. Primary and cleanup failures remain visible together; a tree that cannot be safely removed is retained with its path. The ordinary installer’s existing post-install backup-cleanup limitation remains.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Configured local CAS tree publication (unreleased)
New local CAS definitions can select recursive tree publication through the named registry. Directory selection is independent of full metadata placement:
remotes:
  local:
    snapshots:
      path: ../snapshot-store
      structure: cas
      manifest: auto
      manifest-style: tree
build:
  dest:
    snapshots:
      content: [raw, output]
Omitted content selects eligible non-cache declared labels. Explicit null, false or an empty list selects none; build subsets cannot enable excluded labels. auto means remote for this CAS writer. remote stores complete tree objects and snapshot metadata beside file objects; project stores that metadata under the project; both requires both copies. File objects always remain in the configured store. A small project reference is retained for every successful publication, including remote placement. That reference is not itself a complete archive.
Raw objects, directory objects and snapshot/reference records use first-two- characters/rest-of-hash fan-out. Identical directory contents share a root across labels and versions. Snapshot version associations are separate immutable records. There is no inferred timestamp or mutable discovery index. Existing blobs are verified before reuse. Required graphs precede full references; the small project reference is written last. Errors after provider entry retain the local release and distribution evidence. both is not a cross-location atomic transaction: partial references/objects may remain and errors say so. Nothing is garbage- collected or rolled back from a published store automatically.
Previously accepted path/structure/content/inspect CAS definitions keep their legacy flat JSON identities and plural .projr/manifests.csv ledger. Name-list selection still works; mapping subsets preserve legacy label spelling. To opt into new trees, remove the legacy inspect field and explicitly select tree if desired. No old manifest is reinterpreted or moved.
The first publication slice added tree storage. Explicit named-ID recovery and local CAS flat CSV/JSON histories are described below. Automatic snapshot lookup remains deferred. Legacy inspect belongs only to the old definition; new manifest-format choices are validated against style. Ordinary local/GitHub flat histories are also implemented below, alongside compatible CSV/VERSION metadata; Ordinary local and GitHub tree metadata are described below.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Explicit configured tree readers
Named v1 snapshot verification and single-label restore now consider the full remote and project metadata namespaces independently of current write placement or style. Current upload content does not hide an explicit historical snapshot. All present full copies must verify; absence is distinct from corruption. Readers do not need the old project ledger, root CSV or small project reference.
Selection remains exact title/ID/label, not an automatic newest-version policy. Existing graph limits and guarded installation are reused. Legacy flat IDs are not recast as v1 tree IDs; the compatibility reader below restores their original format. Local CAS flat runtime is described below; ordinary/GitHub flat histories are implemented below; Ordinary local and GitHub tree metadata are described below.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Recover existing flat CAS snapshots
The explicit remote verify / remote restore –snapshot commands also read the original flat JSON snapshots in manifests/<id>.json. Their IDs remain BLAKE3 of the original JSON bytes; they are never reinterpreted as pure content-tree IDs. Responses identify snapshot_kind as legacy-flat or tree-v1.
The reader validates metadata, portable names and every referenced object before using the same guarded staging/installer as trees. Old snapshots remain usable after the remote’s current write style changes, without a project CSV or legacy ledger. Stored metadata, IDs, objects, VERSION and history are never rewritten.
Legacy snapshots record files but not empty directories or permissions. Recovery does not invent that missing history. Unsafe path aliases, traversal, corrupt or missing content and conflicting same-ID namespace entries fail explicitly before destination changes. Metadata is bounded at 16 MiB and 100,000 file entries, with the existing portable path bounds. Ordinary root manifest.csv remains separate.
Automatic snapshot discovery remains deferred; ordinary local and GitHub tree metadata are described below; ordinary/GitHub flat formats are implemented below; this is compatibility recovery, not a format conversion or migration.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Flat history in local CAS
New local CAS remotes can save a readable CSV or JSON history instead of a directory-tree manifest:
remotes:
  local:
    snapshots:
      path: ../snapshot-store
      structure: cas
      manifest-style: flat
      manifest-format: csv
      manifest: remote
build:
  dest:
    snapshots:
      content: [raw, output]
The labels must already be declared. For flat style, csv is the default; json is also available. Both automatically reuse an earlier complete inventory for the same logical folder when later contents are identical, including a reversion to older contents. The later version points directly to that earlier complete version, never a chain. A changed version records all current file memberships, including additions, removals and renamed paths.
CSV is one rectangular table with a header and repeated label/version columns. In Excel, filtering a reference version shows the earlier ref_version to inspect; it does not automatically expand that earlier listing. All earlier complete rows remain in the same history file. Plain CSV/JSON retains literal full file hashes. Optional csv-dedupe-file/json-dedupe-file modes replace repeated hashes with a bundled file dictionary while retaining every file path. These modes are off by default. They are not omitted-file deltas, and no size/speed advantage is promised.
Files are stored once by their BLAKE3 content hash regardless of manifest format. Full history files live under catalogues/v1/manifest.csv or manifest.json; opt-in dictionary files use manifest-dedupe-file.csv/json. Existing root manifest.csv keeps its separate projr-compatible MD5 schema and is unchanged.
auto means remote for CAS. project/remote/both selects full history placement; a small project snapshot binding is always retained. Flat bindings connect the version and selected labels to inventory hashes, independently of serialization or dictionary IDs. They are not directory-tree object IDs. Full immutable refs use flat-snapshots/v1/<first2>/<rest62>.json; small project refs use references/flat-v1/<first2>/<rest62>.json. No unnecessary tree objects are written.
History replacement is atomic per file. Decoded previous label/version contents are never overwritten; divergent histories or conflicting same-version retries fail. Identical per-label retries do not duplicate rows, and missing labels can resume a partial write. Switching format preserves older files/readability and uses the longest compatible decoded history; dictionary IDs do not define it. Codec limits fail explicitly rather than truncating history.
The authoritative history read through replacement/reference publication holds the existing cooperative claim at <store>/.proj/build.lock. Unknown/stale claims fail closed and only an owned claim is removed; there is no automatic process killing or stale-claim cleanup. Raw immutable objects may be copied before that claim. Required history copies precede full snapshot refs, then the small project ref. both is not a cross-location transaction: errors can leave objects or an updated first history copy. Retry can finish the remaining copy.
Explicit verify/restore resolves version references/dictionaries, checks inventory hashes and actual raw bytes, and uses the existing guarded installer. The result reports snapshot_kind: flat-catalogue-v1. Old tree and legacy-flat IDs stay distinct and readable, regardless of the current write style. A small binding alone is not a backup. Empty directories are recorded by this new format, unlike legacy flat.
These manifest-format controls apply to local CAS and the ordinary local/GitHub flat histories described below. Ordinary providers retain compatible CSV/VERSION metadata alongside the new histories. CAS trees default to fixed v1 JSON; explicit manifest-format: json is valid there, while CSV/dictionary choices require flat style. Null/unknown modes fail instead of silently choosing a default.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Ordinary local history integration (development source)
Ordinary latest/archive data keeps its existing directory layout; new flat catalogues do not copy files into objects. A distinct versioned local binding records each logical folder’s inventory hash, relative physical payload path, empty flag and existing VERSION advertisement. Its ID is a snapshot binding, not a pure content root. Small project references persist with remote-only full metadata. One archive payload may serve several build-version observations. Mutable latest storage cannot promise recovery of older overwritten content.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
GitHub flat history integration (development source)
GitHub full catalogue/history and snapshot bindings share the versioned projcli-manifests-v1.zip asset; data stays in the ordinary ZIP layout. Bindings include frozen repository/tag and the actual payload asset, separate from the build-version inventory. Exact prepared ZIP observations preserve existing packaging semantics rather than inventing empty directories. Disk-backed private records avoid retaining full metadata buffers for every target at once.
Every required HTTP write and full project copy precedes small project references. Original asset-ID checks protect against replacing an already changed history; they do not establish cross-writer or crash atomicity. No CAS objects, new credential mechanism, live user-data test or broad snapshot discovery is introduced.

Flat CAS placement continuity
Configured flat CAS separates known history read locations from selected full-copy destinations. Project/store histories must be compatible prefixes before hooks, and publication rereads them under the existing store claim. Only selected copies change; old files/IDs remain. The public explicit-bases flat publication API keeps its signature/scope. Tree and legacy formats are unchanged.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Ordinary local directory trees (development source)
Tree metadata and storage structure remain independent. Ordinary local tree style keeps normal folder/archive data and stores only content-derived directory objects under the selected metadata roots. The exact existing DirectoryTree v1 codec and sharded path convention are reused; native CAS over identical payload membership yields the same root.
The readable catalogue is a companion lookup/inspection projection, excluded from pure root identity and checked against graph membership. It deliberately duplicates names/hashes; no speed/size improvement is claimed. The new ordinary tree binding schema carries tree alongside the distinct inventory_hash, physical path, empty flag and existing VERSION advertisement. Earlier flat bindings do not gain fields or change IDs. No legacy reinterpretation, GC or raw object-store conversion is performed.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
GitHub tree metadata integration
Ordinary GitHub data remains latest/archive ZIP assets. Tree metadata reuses the v1 pure directory codec and first-two/rest sharding, with a distinct projcli.github-tree-snapshot.v1 binding. A readable JSON catalogue deliberately duplicates membership for inspection and existing immutable-version lookup; its inventory hash must equal the graph’s expanded membership. No raw CAS object path is followed for ordinary payload bytes.
The existing bounded metadata bundle now allowlists directory objects as well as histories/bindings. Validate all object identities before controlled graph reads; missing, corrupt or contradictory metadata fails before HTTP mutation. Private disk-backed graphs are prepared before uploads and copied to selected full project locations only after all required HTTP succeeds. Small references remain last. Flat IDs and earlier nodes survive style changes. No compression/performance, multi-target atomicity or new snapshot-discovery guarantee is implied.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Bounded M3 release evidence
The final pinned gate retains actual native CAS stores and exact recovered files after a two-build analysis plus ordinary backup. It recovers by explicit snapshot ID into a fresh project, then probes missing/corrupt content and malformed metadata without modifying good targets. A separate Rust witness checks retained snapshots against recovered bytes and ordinary CSV hashes. Broader discovery and performance work remains deferred; complete platform suites cover writer, interruption, retry and all format/placement boundaries. Passing this gate is source evidence; release/install verification remains separate.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Legacy lookup publication coordination
Raw-JSON legacy IDs and the headerless four-column .projr/manifests.csv lookup remain readable and writable. Publication now owns cooperative claims for both the physical store and project legacy-ledger root, with sorted/deduplicated physical coordination roots. A store-only claim cannot protect two stores updating one project ledger. The distinct ledger root avoids reentering the project build claim.
Parse existing lookup rows without rewriting them, then append only if the exact version/label/digest tuple is new. Source pre-scan precedes coordination writes; claims cover authoritative lookup read through complete metadata/index writes. Different digests for the same version/label retain legacy behavior. No format, identity, garbage-collection or retention redesign is part of this safety fix.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Experimental Xet investigation
See the experimental local candidate for the pinned optional engine, independent reconstruction verification and upstream suitability limits. It does not change supported storage defaults or reinterpret existing CAS IDs. Configured selection/GitHub complete-store transfer remain pending. The private preservation sync encountered a GitHub workflows-permission restriction; source copy/build independence is not yet established. No credential workaround is used.

title: Command exit status
text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.


proj build-dev --project demo --non-interactive
--non-interactive disables the CLI’s own prompts and automatic R-package installation, including when PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL=true. Missing dependencies produce an error. Script, hook and renderer runners and controlled R dependency probes receive closed stdin. The mode is inherited by managed children as PROJ_NON_INTERACTIVE=true.
Initialization still performs requested operations using its existing defaults. This flag does not choose project markers, change configuration precedence or define a structured result protocol. Third-party code remains responsible for its own behavior after receiving EOF.
